foodmfg.name: Food and beverage manufacturing
foodmfg.desc: Bakeries, breweries, wineries, meat and dairy processing, packaged food
profile: Product recall plan documented and tested?
Sell to supermarkets or large retailers with their own supplier terms?

gen: Customer and supplier dependence
One supermarket or distributor may account for most sales. A lost contract or recall can end the business. Ask about concentration.
Ingredients and allergens
Source of ingredients, allergen management and label accuracy. Labelling errors are the most common recall.
liab: Product liability and contamination
Contamination, foreign objects and illness. Check product liability and contamination cover, the export territorial limit and the recall cover.
bi: Key ingredients, packaging and seasonal peaks. Check dependent property cover and the indemnity period against re-commissioning time.
machinery: Single-line production, spares and lead times for imported machinery. Check breakdown cover and the effect on spoilage.

manufacturing.name: Metal fabrication and general manufacturing
manufacturing.desc: Engineering workshops, fabrication, plastics, packaging and light manufacturing
profile: Chemicals, gases or flammable materials used?

gen: Customer industries and end use
Components used in aircraft, medical devices, vehicles or buildings carry higher exposure. Ask where the product ends up.
liab: Product liability and defect costs
Failure of a component can cause loss well beyond the part itself. Check product liability, recall and the cost of replacing or repairing defective work.
Contracts with large customers
Supply agreements often require specific limits, indemnities and warranties. Ask who drafts them and what the limit of liability is.
mdamage: Welding, grinding, machining oils and dust. Ask about hot work controls, extraction, flammable storage and fire detection.
pi: If you design or specify products, check cover for design errors and for work to customer drawings.

signage.name: Signage and printing
signage.desc: Sign makers, installers, vehicle wraps, large-format print and promotional products
profile: Own or hire EWPs, scissor lifts or cranes?
Signs wired by a registered electrician?
Part of a franchise or buying group?

gen: Installation versus workshop
What share of work is on customer sites, at what height, and who does it? Installation turns a manufacturing risk into a liability risk.
Franchise requirements
Does the franchisor require specific limits, extensions or named interests? Check the franchise agreement.
liab: Care, custody and control
Customer property in your care: vehicles being wrapped, buildings you are working on. Check the care, custody and control extension and its limit.
Falling signs and wind
Structural design, engineering sign-off, fixings and inspection. A sign falling from a building is the large-loss scenario.
Copyright and defamation
Copied logos or artwork, wrong content or offensive print. Check whether media or IP cover is needed.
pi: Spelling errors, wrong colours or dimensions. Reprints are a common claim. Check whether redoing the work is excluded.
machinery: Large-format printers and cutters. Service contracts, replacement lead times and spares.

timber.name: Sawmills, timber and furniture
timber.desc: Timber processing, sawmills, treatment plants and furniture manufacture

mdamage: Dust, offcuts, drying kilns and outdoor stacks. Ask about extraction, housekeeping, fire detection, separation of stacks and water supply.
liab: Treatment and product failure
Wrongly treated timber that rots or fails. Check product liability and the exclusion for faulty workmanship or material.
statutory: Saws, planers and conveyors cause serious injuries. Guarding, lockout and training records.

wholesale.name: Wholesalers and importers
wholesale.desc: Wholesale distribution, importers and trading companies
profile: Sell to major retailers with specific supplier terms?

liab: Importer’s liability
If the manufacturer cannot be pursued, the importer is liable. Check recall cover, supplier warranties and overseas jurisdictions.
cargo: Marine cargo from the supplier’s door to your warehouse, delivery terms and who carries the risk at each stage.
bi: One supplier or one port can stop trading. Check dependent suppliers and transit delays.

dairyfarm.name: Dairy farms
dairyfarm.desc: Dairy farming, dairy support and sharemilking
profile: Effluent system and discharge consent compliant?
Support block or run-off leased or owned elsewhere?
Staff or contract milkers living on the farm?

mdamage: Dairy shed, vat and effluent plant
Replacement value of the milking plant, vat, effluent and irrigation systems. Check cover for loss of milk from vat breakdown and power failure.
gen: Herd and livestock cover
Livestock cover for death by accident, fire and flood, and consider TB, calving risks and transit. Check sums insured against current values.
liab: Stock on roads and neighbour claims
Stock straying onto roads and damage to neighbouring land. Check farm liability and pollution cover for effluent.

sheepbeef.name: Sheep, beef and cropping
sheepbeef.desc: Sheep and beef farms, arable cropping, deer and mixed farms
profile: Shearing, contractors or seasonal workers used?
Hay or baleage stored in sheds?
Controlled burning or machinery use in dry periods?

mdamage: Hay barns, woolsheds and workshops. Spontaneous combustion of stored hay, machinery fires and distance from fire brigades.
liab: Fire spread and rural fire
Fires started by machinery or burning off can spread to neighbours. Check liability for fire fighting costs and rural fire authority claims.
Contractors and workers
Shearers, fencers and contractors working on the farm. Check agreements, ACC levies and insurance certificates.

horticulture.name: Orchards, vineyards and nurseries
horticulture.desc: Kiwifruit, apples, grapes, vegetables, nurseries and packhouses
profile: Hail nets or frost protection in place?
Seasonal workers or contract labour used?

gen: Crop and weather cover
Hail, frost and wind risks, crop insurance options and sums insured. Ask about revenue per hectare and the market risk.
Seasonal labour
Seasonal workers, accommodation and contractors. Check agreements, health and safety and worker accommodation exposure.
mdamage: Hail nets, shelter belts, trellis and irrigation. Check replacement values, cover for wind and snow damage, and whether crop and infrastructure are insured.
liab: Spray drift and food safety
Spray drift to neighbours, residue claims and food safety recalls. Check chemical records and product liability for exported produce.

forestry.name: Forestry and logging
forestry.desc: Forestry management, harvesting, logging and silviculture
profile: Forest area managed or harvested annually (hectares)
Contract crews or owner operators used?
Fire season controls and equipment on site?

gen: Contractor structure
Harvesting is often done by contract crews. Check contractor agreements, insurance certificates and who controls the site.
High-risk work
Felling, steep terrain and machinery operation are among the most dangerous work in NZ. Ask about fatalities, near misses, training and critical controls.
liab: Fire and runoff
Forest fires spread to neighbouring land and slash, sediment and logs can damage property downstream. Check liability for fire fighting costs and runoff claims.
mdamage: Harvesters, skidders and log trucks are high value. Check basis of cover, transit, rollover and theft.
